Abstract.AbstractText: The reduced number of sensors in sparse arrays create high peak sidelobe levels (PSLs). This letter compares the PSLs of minimum redundancy arrays (MRAs), minimum hole arrays (MHAs), and co-prime sensor arrays (CSAs) (conventionally beamformed and product processed) with fully populated uniform linear arrays (ULAs) as a function of aperture using both numerical simulations and experimental data. This letter finds that PSLs of MRAs, MHAs, and conventionally processed CSAs are much higher than the ULA PSL and are largely insensitive to aperture extension. In contrast, CSA product processing decreases the PSL with increasing aperture, eventually matching the ULA PSL.
